title: Unique
subtitle: Unique 可以表示『獨一無二、有明顯特色、不尋常、非凡、無可匹敵，或具有個別性』。 這些意思強度不同。最重要的是分清 literal uniqueness、distinctiv
description: Unique 可以表示『獨一無二、有明顯特色、不尋常、非凡、無可匹敵，或具有個別性』。 這些意思強度不同。最重要的是分清 literal uniqueness、distinctiveness、rarity、excellence、comparative superiority、individual character。

words.example: The building has a distinctive curved roof.
words.exampleZh: 這座建築有一個很有特色的弧形屋頂。

exercises.original: The product has a unique visual identity.
exercises.zh: 產品有一個獨特的視覺識別。
exercises.upgrade: A. Distinctive · 獨特的；有特色的

options.explanation: Distinctive ✓ — clearly different in a noticeable or recognisable way. Here, recognisable characteristic style is central. That makes Distinctive the most precise replacement for this particular sense of unique.

Unusual — different from what is normal or common. This only means uncommon and does not necessarily imply strong distinctiveness or superiority. The decisive clue is that recognisable characteristic style is central.

Individual — having a character or quality particular to one person or thing. This emphasises personal or particular identity rather than rarity or one-of-a-kind status. The decisive clue is that recognisable characteristic style is central.
Rare — not common or frequently found. This describes low frequency, not uniqueness. The decisive clue is that recognisable characteristic style is central.
Different — not the same. This is much weaker and only says something is not the same. The decisive clue is that recognisable characteristic style is central.
Special — important, unusual, or valued. This is broad and can mean important, valued, or unusual without implying uniqueness. The decisive clue is that recognisable characteristic style is central.

Unusual — different from what is normal or common. This only means uncommon and does not necessarily imply strong distinctiveness or superiority. The decisive clue is that each person has their own perspective.
Rare — not common or frequently found. This describes low frequency, not uniqueness. The decisive clue is that each person has their own perspective.
Special — important, unusual, or valued. This is broad and can mean important, valued, or unusual without implying uniqueness. The decisive clue is that each person has their own perspective.
Original — new, creative, or originating from a source. This focuses on creativity or source, not necessarily uniqueness. The decisive clue is that each person has their own perspective.

Individual ✓ — having a character or quality particular to one person or thing. Here, each person has their own perspective. That makes Individual the most precise replacement for this particular sense of unique.

words.meaning: 與眾不同的；不同於任何其他的
words.example: The landscape offers an experience unlike any other in the region.
words.exampleZh: 這片景觀帶來區內其他地方都沒有的獨特體驗。

exercises.original: The region offers a unique cultural experience.

exercises.upgrade: A. Unlike any other · 與眾不同的；不同於任何其他的

options.explanation: Unlike any other ✓ — different from all comparable alternatives. Here, expanded emphasis on strong distinctiveness. That makes Unlike any other the most precise replacement for this particular sense of unique.

Distinctive — clearly different in a noticeable or recognisable way. This stresses recognisability but not literal uniqueness or unmatched quality. The decisive clue is that expanded emphasis on strong distinctiveness.

One-of-a-kind — the only one of its kind. This implies literal or near-literal uniqueness and can be too strong for merely distinctive features. The decisive clue is that expanded emphasis on strong distinctiveness.
Rare — not common or frequently found. This describes low frequency, not uniqueness. The decisive clue is that expanded emphasis on strong distinctiveness.
Different — not the same. This is much weaker and only says something is not the same. The decisive clue is that expanded emphasis on strong distinctiveness.
Special — important, unusual, or valued. This is broad and can mean important, valued, or unusual without implying uniqueness. The decisive clue is that expanded emphasis on strong distinctiveness.

exercises.original: The building has a unique design.
exercises.zh: 這座建築有一個與眾不同的設計。
exercises.upgrade: B. Unlike any other · 與眾不同的；不同於任何其他的

options.explanation: Distinctive — clearly different in a noticeable or recognisable way. This stresses recognisability but not literal uniqueness or unmatched quality. The decisive clue is that the paraphrase explicitly compares it with all alternatives.

Unlike any other ✓ — different from all comparable alternatives. Here, the paraphrase explicitly compares it with all alternatives. That makes Unlike any other the most precise replacement for this particular sense of unique.

One-of-a-kind — the only one of its kind. This implies literal or near-literal uniqueness and can be too strong for merely distinctive features. The decisive clue is that the paraphrase explicitly compares it with all alternatives.
Rare — not common or frequently found. This describes low frequency, not uniqueness. The decisive clue is that the paraphrase explicitly compares it with all alternatives.
Different — not the same. This is much weaker and only says something is not the same. The decisive clue is that the paraphrase explicitly compares it with all alternatives.

Special — important, unusual, or valued. This is broad and can mean important, valued, or unusual without implying uniqueness. The decisive clue is that the paraphrase explicitly compares it with all alternatives.

exercises.original: The festival creates a unique atmosphere.
exercises.zh: 節慶營造出與眾不同的氣氛。

falseSynonyms.zh: 罕見 ≠ unique rare 只表示少見，不等於只有一個。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON Rare is about frequency, not uniqueness.

falseSynonyms.zh: 不同 ≠ unique different 只表示有差異，程度可能很小。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON Different is much weaker.

falseSynonyms.zh: 原創 ≠ unique original 強調創意或來源，不一定獨一無二。
特別 ≠ unique special 很廣，可只表示重要或受重視。
專有／獨家 ≠ unique exclusive 強調限制存取或獨家權利，不等於本質獨特。
只在卓越 sense 接近 exceptional 強調非常出色，不只是不同。
只在『有特色』sense 接近 distinctive 可很有特色，但不一定獨一無二。
詞性陷阱 unique 是形容詞；uniquely 是副詞。
